entry.title: The Borodin--Kostochka Conjecture for Two Classes of Diamond-Free Graphs
entry.summary: We prove the Borodin--Kostochka conjecture for $(\mathrm{diamond},L_4)$-free graphs and $(\mathrm{diamond},K_5^+)$-free graphs, where $L_4$ is obtained from $K_4$ by attaching a path of length two to one clique vertex, and $K_5^+$ is obtained from $K_5$ by adding a vertex adjacent to exactly one clique vertex. The proof uses structural properties of maximum cliques in diamond-free vertex-critical graphs with $χ=Δ$.

entry.title: A counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
entry.summary: A ring is right pure semisimple if every right module is a direct sum of finitely generated modules, and the pure semisimplicity conjecture asserts that every such ring is of finite representation type. In this article, a division ring extension $H\subseteq T$ is constructed such that the bimodule ${}_HT_T$ has right dimension sequence $(1,2,2,2,\dots)$ and $T$ is infinite-dimensional as a left $H$-space. The division ring $T$ is the union of the fraction division rings of the nearest-neighbour quantum Laurent algebras with parameter $1/2$, and $H$ is the image of $T$ under a compatible family of conjugations. The extension is controlled by right bases of every length and by two-sided flags of adjacent division subrings, which identify all iterated right duals up to explicit twists. It follows that the triangular ring $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}H&T\\0&T\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type, so that the pure semisimplicity conjecture fails.

The repository includes an earlier manuscript snapshot corresponding to the formalization. entry.title: A proof of the Murty--Simon conjecture on diameter-$2$-critical graphs
entry.summary: The Murty-Simon conjecture states that every $n$-vertex diameter-$2$-critical graph has at most $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ edges, with equality only for the balanced complete bipartite graph. Using regularity methods, Füredi proved this for all sufficiently large $n$ (specifically, $n$ greater than a tower of $2$'s of height roughly $10^{14}$). We present a proof of the Murty-Simon conjecture that works for all $n$. A proof of the $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ bound was originally found by AI; we simplified this proof and extended its ideas to get a proof of the full conjecture.

entry.title: On a Conjecture of Fiedorowicz
entry.summary: Fiedorowicz conjectured that every finite simply connected CW complex is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite monoid. We prove this conjecture. Our main construction takes a finite monoid M and a map from a finite connected CW complex into the classifying space of M, and produces a new finite monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to the mapping cone of the given map. Applying this construction successively to the attaching maps of a finite CW model proves the result. As an explicit example of the algorithm, we construct a 1795-element monoid whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to two dimensional complex projective space.

entry.title: Enumeration of zero-sum subsequences: A proof of Bialostocki-Lotspeich conjecture
entry.summary: Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n\ge 2$, and let $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_{\ell}$ be a sequence over $C_n$, with repetitions allowed. We denote by $\mathsf N_0^n(S)$ the number of subsets $I\subseteq[1,\ell]$ with $|I|=n$ and $\sum_{i\in I}g_i=0$. A conjecture proposed by Bialostocki and Lotspeich in 1992 states that $$\mathsf N_0^n(S)\ge \binom{\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor}{n}+ \binom{\lceil |S|/2\rceil}{n}.$$ Several partial results toward this conjecture are known. In this paper, we prove this conjecture completely.

entry.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in eight dimensions over the field with two elements
entry.summary: Fuglede's conjecture in a finite abelian group says that a nonempty subset tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral, meaning that the space of complex-valued functions on the subset has an orthogonal basis consisting of restrictions of group characters. We prove the conjecture in the eight-dimensional vector space over the field with two elements. In fact, every spectral set and every tile in this space has a tiling complement which is a linear subspace. We first prove that the Fourier support of a nonempty proper subset of density different from one half contains a two-dimensional subspace. Consequently, every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This gives a simpler proof of Kadowaki's dimension-seven result, replacing his use of the classification of Hadamard matrices of order 32 by the classical five classes of order 16. Our dimension-eight proof uses exact finite verifications involving Hadamard matrices of order 32 and perfect codes of length 15. We include the proofs of the reductions used from Kadowaki's preprint, so that neither positive result depends on his dimension-seven theorem. Finally, we give an elementary spectral example of density one eighth in dimension nine whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. Thus, the Fourier-support argument at quarter density does not extend in this form to eighth density. Dimension nine is the only case still unresolved over the field with two elements, and this obstruction shows why the present Fourier-support method cannot resolve it as it stands.
entry.arxiv:comment: 22 pages. Programs, data, certificates, and verification logs are included as ancillary files. Standalone treatment of selected results from the preliminary preprint arXiv:2610.30712, with a new, simpler dimension-seven proof

entry.title: Proofs of strong forms of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture and a complex analogue
entry.summary: We prove two universality theorems for neural networks consisting of a single neuron. First we prove a strong form of the Bovdi--Geche universality conjecture on neurons over finite fields, where the activation function is a certain modification of the discrete logarithm, using the Weil bound on multiplicative character sums over finite fields. Then we show a generalisation of Aizenberg's universality theorem for complex binary neurons with a weight vector independent of the target function, positively answering another question in the literature. The proof of the latter uses an equidistribution theorem for the dilates of certain maps into tori.

entry.title: On Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges of compact adjoint orbits
entry.summary: We settle Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges associated with compact adjoint orbits of complex reductive Lie algebras, including its original formulation in terms of the inner product $B_θ$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let $K$ be a connected compact Lie group whose Lie algebra is a compact real form of $\mathfrak{g}$. For any $x\in\mathfrak{g}$ and any complex linear functional $f\in\mathfrak{g}^*$, we prove that $\{ f( \operatorname{Ad} (k) x): k \in K \}$ is star-shaped about zero. In the reductive case, the star center is given by the value of $f$ on the central component of $x$, which coincides with the $B_θ$-pairing of the central components in Tam's original formulation. Our proof is uniform for all complex semisimple Lie algebras. Indeed, using the adjoint Casimir operator, we show that all coordinate functions of the orbit map share a common Laplace eigenvalue; we then use a nodal-hypersurface argument to prove star-shapedness for complex-valued functions in a single eigenspace. The geometric argument relies on a two-sided hypersurface-separation property, which holds whenever the first real cohomology group vanishes. In particular, we do not need simple connectivity or real analyticity. More generally, for finite-dimensional representations of compact connected semisimple Lie groups, we establish star-shapedness whenever the nonfixed component of the orbit vector belongs to a single positive Casimir eigenspace.

entry.title: Proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: an exposition
entry.summary: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$ is exactly $\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor$. We present a streamlined variant of the proof of this conjecture recently announced by OpenAI (2026). Although the original proof is relatively short, it is quite difficult to follow. We simplify several steps and provide a concise and accessible exposition of the proof. We also combine this new result with known reductions to determine the crossing numbers of several other graph families.

entry.title: Graham's rearrangement conjecture in finite abelian groups
entry.summary: Graham conjectured in 1971 that every subset of the nonzero elements of a prime cyclic group admits an ordering with pairwise distinct nonempty partial sums. Recently, the work of Pham and Sauermann, together with earlier results, settled this conjecture for all sufficiently large primes. In this paper, we prove that there is an absolute integer $n_0$ such that every subset $S\subseteq G\setminus\{0\}$ of a finite abelian group with $|S|\ge n_0$ admits such an ordering, which also solves a conjecture of Alspach and Liversidge for all sufficiently large sets. A key ingredient of our proof is a sufficient condition via additive dimension: If $|S|=n$ and $S$ contains a dissociated subset of size at least $Ω((\log n)^2/\log\log n)$, then $S$ has an ordering in which no proper nonempty interval of consecutive terms sums to zero. This bound is within a factor of $O(\log n/\log\log n)$ of the smallest possible additive dimension of an $n$-element set.

entry.title: Counting Admissible Sets of Integers: A Proof of the Erdős--Nicolas--Sárközy Conjecture
entry.summary: A finite set of positive integers is admissible if any two of its subsets with the same sum have the same cardinality. In 1991, Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy conjectured that $\log a(N)\asymp\sqrt N$, where $a(N)$ denotes the number of nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. We prove this conjecture by showing that there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that $\exp(c\sqrt N)\le a(N)\le\exp(C\sqrt N)$ for every integer $N\ge4$. The same bounds hold for the number of admissible sets with maximum $N$. For the upper bound, we show that every sufficiently large admissible set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ contains a subset of proportional size whose doubling constant is $O(N/|A|^2)$.

entry.title: The Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets
entry.summary: We prove that for all $n\ge3$ and $r\ge2$, the Lee ball $B_n(r)$ does not tile $\Z^n$ by translations, resolving the Golomb--Welch conjecture for arbitrary centre sets and completing the existence classification of perfect Lee codes in $\Z^n$. The proof combines translation-invariant averaging, boundary contact identities, and integer moment inequalities with coefficient comparisons in stable symmetric functions. Consequently, we obtain finite local obstructions, strict Banach density gaps for packings and coverings, and the nonexistence of exact measurable Lee-ball towers. In the lattice specialization, our result classifies the attainability of the Lee bound for even-degree abelian Cayley graphs, excludes normal topological coverings and Galois graph coverings for Lee-ball completions, and gives a strict node bound for lattice cubature as well as the nonexistence of subgroup-indexed orthogonal exponential bases on $B_n(r)$.

entry.title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
entry.summary: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. For the converse, an endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one gives rise to a family of holonomic $A_2$-modules over finite fields. One needs to lift this family to an $A_2$-module in characteristic zero with the prescribed arithmetic support. The existence of such a lift is a special case of Kontsevich's conjecture on holonomic $\mathcal D$-modules with prescribed arithmetic support. We prove that in this special situation such a lift is unique whenever it exists. If these lifts exists for every endomorphism with Jacobian one, then $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ implies $\mathrm{JC}_2$. For every $n\ge 3$, we construct a Lagrangian subvariety of $T^*\mathbb{A}^n$ that provides a counterexample to Kontsevich's conjecture. The counterexamples arise from the graph of a noninvertible symplectic endomorphism of $\mathbb A^4$ constructed by Long. We also present a different strategy for lifting $\mathcal D$-modules associated with a Jacobian-one endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ to characteristic zero via ultraproducts and show that the existence of a characteristic-zero lift in this setting is equivalent to the uniform boundedness of the Berest--Wilson invariants of these $A_2$-modules, regarded as left $A_1$-modules. Finally, we study two other conjectures of Kontsevich on arithmetic support, giving a counterexample to one and partial results on the other.

entry.title: Proof of the Langberg-Médard Multiple Unicast Conjecture
entry.summary: Let $\mathcal{N}=(V,A,S, R)$ be a directed network, where $D=(V,A)$ is a digraph, $S=\{s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of senders, and $R=\{r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k\}\subseteq V$ is a set of receivers. We prove that if, for each $1\le j \le k$, there exist $k$ pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in $D$, one from each $s_i$ to $r_j$, then the underlying undirected network of ${\cal N}$, with unit capacities, admits a feasible $(s_1,s_2,\ldots,s_k)$-$(r_1,r_2,\ldots,r_k)$ multiflow of value $1$ for each pair $(s_i,r_i)$, $i=1,2,\ldots,k$. This establishes the multiple unicast conjecture proposed by Langberg and Médard in 2009.

entry.title: A proof of Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture
entry.summary: We prove Wang's planar D-coloring conjecture. A D-coloring of a graph is a proper edge coloring in which every subgraph isomorphic to $K_4$ minus an edge is rainbow. Wang conjectured that every planar graph of maximum degree $Δ$ has a D-coloring with 9 colors if $Δ=4$, 10 colors if $Δ=5$, and $2Δ-1$ colors if $Δ\ge 6$. Hu, Kong and Wang proved the cases $Δ\le 5$ and $Δ\ge 33$. We prove the sharp bound $2Δ-1$ for every $Δ\ge 6$, settling the remaining cases. The proof uses discharging; the case $Δ=6$ is computer-assisted.
entry.arxiv:comment: 21 pages. Ancillary files contain the certificates and verification scripts for the computer-assisted case of maximum degree 6

entry.title: A Short Proof of Zhang's Conjecture on Stack-Sortable Permutations
entry.summary: We give a short proof of Zhang's conjecture that the number of stack-sortable permutations of length $n + 1$ which end in their smallest element is equal to the $n$-th Motzkin number.

entry.title: Finite stabilization, socle extensions, and Faith's conjecture
entry.summary: We give a length-two counterexample to the unrestricted product comparison in Bergman's Question 3.1, positive criteria for quasi-injective common modules, and a semidirect-product version of Question 3.2. For semiprimary right self-injective rings, the countable hull construction yields a cyclic two-layer witness, its Baer class, and an opposite-side extension obstruction. We apply this construction over the square-zero ring of the counterexample. The hull quotient of a countable sum of injectives is the endomorphism space modulo finite-rank maps, and computes the full socle-radical defect of a countable product of the regular module. This gives a second counterexample with free cyclic family factors. The original length-two product embeds its defect in the same quotient through an explicit intersection, and all associated extension classes arise from one specified Baer class. The general Faith conjecture remains unresolved.

entry.title: A counterexample to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions
entry.summary: It is well known that the sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^n$ has algebraic degree at most $n/2$ for even $n\ge 4$. Tokareva conjectured that the converse holds: every Boolean function with degree at most $n/2$ can be written as a sum of two bent functions. The conjecture has been verified for even $n\leq 6$ and for several special classes of Boolean functions. We disprove this conjecture by showing that $x_1x_2(x_3x_4+x_5x_6+x_7x_8)$ is not a sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^8$. We extend this construction to obtain counterexamples in every even dimension $n\ge 8$. Using Shaporenko's reduction, we also obtain explicit counterexamples to Tokareva's derivative conjecture in every even dimension $n\ge 10$.
entry.arxiv:comment: The counterexamples and proofs in this paper were obtained through large-scale automated reasoning with LLM agents while solving Problem~10 in NSUCRYPTO~2026 (MiniMax M3.1-Flash-Preview, 19 rounds of up to 100 independent agents between 12 and 18 October 2026, 1889 reports in all), paired with 8 rounds of independent audits (227 reports)

entry.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
entry.summary: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We prove that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\left\lfloor4(n-1)/3\right\rfloor$ edges. The proof combines Pammer's computer-assisted verification of the conjecture for graphs on at most twelve vertices with a discharging argument in suitable plane and projective-plane embeddings.

entry.title: Two refined Wilf-equivalences for patterns of length 4 and a conjecture on Dumont permutations of the first kind
entry.summary: We construct a bijection between $2143$-avoiding and $3421$-avoiding permutations that preserves the descent top set and the ascent top set and reverses the left-to-right order of the peaks. This bijection allows us to establish a bijection between $1243$-avoiding and $3412$-avoiding permutations with the same properties. These results refine two cases of a conjecture posed by Burstein and prove a conjecture posed by Burstein and Jones.

entry.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_{p}^{d}$ for $p=2,\,d=8$ and $p=11,\,d=3$
entry.summary: Fuglede's conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ says that a nonempty set tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral. We prove the conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_2^8$ and $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ we show more generally that the Fourier support of a nonconstant indicator of density different from one half contains a plane. Consequently every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This supplies one of the dimension-eight reductions left by Kadowaki; the others are completed using classified Hadamard matrices and perfect binary codes. In $\mathbb{F}_2^9$ we prove that every tile is spectral and that every spectral set has power-of-two cardinality. All spectral cardinalities except $64$ are shown to tile, and we give further reductions of the remaining case. We also construct a spectral set of density one eighth whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. For $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$ we extend the geometric method of Fallon, Mayeli, and Villano by using moment identities, polynomial plane profiles, weighted incidence counts, and exact finite computations. The computations and their verification programs are described in the appendices.

entry.title: On Arithmetic-Progression Biases in Random Partitions: Limiting Laws and the Li-Zhao Conjecture
entry.summary: Let $\cR=\{r+jm:j\geq0\}$ and $\cS=\{s+jm:j\geq0\}$ be disjoint arithmetic progressions of positive integers, and choose a partition of $n$ uniformly at random. We determine the limiting probability that the number of parts in $\cR$ is larger than the number of parts in $\cS$. More precisely, if $a=r/m$ and $b=s/m$, then this probability converges to $I_{1/2}(a,b)$, the regularized incomplete beta function. We prove the stronger distributional statement that, after multiplication by the partition saddle-point parameter, the difference of the two numbers of parts converges to $m^{-1}(\log G_b-\log G_a)$, where $G_a$ and $G_b$ are independent gamma variables. The proof uses the Boltzmann conditioning device for random partitions, a $q$-gamma evaluation of the unconditioned characteristic function, and a uniform Fourier estimate showing that conditioning on the total size does not change the limit. We also evaluate the finite-truncation limit studied by Li and Zhao. The two evaluations coincide, proving their conjecture on the commutation of the truncation and large-size limits.
